title: plan.yml: the design plan of a map (the brief at levels L0 to L3), schema v0
description: What a level designer hands over: places, how they connect, what the player does there. No coordinates finer than the plan grid, no faces, no textures per face. The same file is the brief of a calibration build and the plan of a new map.

level.description: How much the plan specifies: L0 pitch, L1 plan, L2 specification, L3 sketch.

pitch.description: L0. One paragraph: what the place is, who lives there, how it is played, its mood.

purpose.description: Why the party comes and what the map is for in its world.

datum.description: What heights are measured from: `arrival` (the default), `sea_level`, or a space id.

spaces.description: Indoor: the rooms, corridors and other spaces. Outdoor: zones and districts. One list, so links, paths and points of interest refer to either.

regions.description: Groups of spaces: wings, quarters, a cave system beside a temple.

links.description: How spaces connect: the room graph or the road graph.

loops.description: Rings in the graph the player can run, and what opens them.

teleport_sets.description: Teleporters that land in one of several places.

sources.description: The links, points of interest or spaces that send the party.

rule.description: How the landing is chosen (random, never the source's own).

lock_groups.description: Locks shared by several links (two doors, one pair of keys spent when the second opens).

links.description: The links that share the lock.

entrances.description: Where the party arrives and leaves.

neighbour.description: The project.yml neighbour this leads to.

neighbours.description: When several routes share the place (one pier for four ships).

facing.description: Compass direction the arriving party faces.

how.description: How it is reached or what it looks like (a mouth at the top of a ramp, a trapdoor).

offset_from.description: Where it lies against another entrance.

variants.description: What it does instead while a condition holds (a door that is a quest giver, then a dungeon, then a house). The first variant whose condition holds applies.

target.description: A neighbour, entrance or space id this leads to in that case.

critical_path.description: The spaces the party passes from arrival to the map's goal, in order.

return_path.description: The way back out, when it differs from the way in.

goals.description: What completing the map means: things reached, taken, killed or set.

story.description: Step of the world's story.yml this goal is.

handed_in_at.description: Where the result is handed in: a neighbour id or a map.

gives.description: What completing it sets: one condition or a list of them.

keys.description: What opens the map's locks and where each comes from. A lock itself is the `condition` of a link.

how.description: chest, floor, actor drop, lever, given by an NPC, another map.

points_of_interest.description: Things with behaviour: wells, fountains, shrines, altars, obelisks, teachers, readable statues, clickable spots.

spaces.description: When the same thing stands in several spaces.

behaviour.description: What it does when used, as a rule.

rule.description: A rule the engine already has, as native:<name> (native:obelisk, native:stat_challenge).

gives.description: What using it sets or gives.

after_use.description: What changes to the eye once used (a tree goes bare).

neighbour.description: A point of interest that leads to another map.

also.description: Other entries (an entrance, a landmark) that are this same object.

variants.description: What it does instead while a condition holds (a door that is a quest giver, then a dungeon, then a house). The first variant whose condition holds applies.

target.description: A neighbour, entrance or space id this leads to in that case.

landmarks.description: What the player steers by and what should be seen from where.

hidden_from.description: Spaces it must not be seen from.

sightlines.description: What the player should see from where.

set_pieces.description: Puzzles, traps and scripted moments as rules: inputs, states, solution. A set piece may span several spaces.

path.description: For something that travels (a trap's lane): the spaces it crosses, in order.

end.description: Which end or side of the space.

period.description: For timed things: game minutes between runs.

mechanisms.description: L2. The inventory of moving and clickable things by kind.

height_bands.description: The map's vertical layers, relative to the arrival.

level.description: A single level instead of a range.

partly.description: Spaces only partly in the band.

states.description: Staged states: what the map shows or hides once a condition holds (a castle rebuilt, a town locked down, a wing sealed).

locks.description: Buildings or spaces whose services and doors stop working.

npc_moves.description: People who change houses with the story.

landform.description: Outdoor: the shape of the land in words and bands (relief, water, coast).

water_share.description: Share of the map that is water.

caps.description: What tops the high ground (snow, bare rock).

rim.description: The land at the map's edge.

atmosphere.description: L2. Sky, light, weather, music and sound in words.

diagram.description: L1: the not-to-scale bubble diagram, as a file beside the plan or as text.

sketch.description: L3. Where the to-scale sketch is: rooms.yml for indoor shells, or an image on the plan grid.

totals.description: Whole-map targets the build is compared with. Use the names `oymap metrics` writes where one exists (sectors, links, loops, doors, floor_area_millions, spawn_points, fixed_actors, lights, decorations, chest_events, secret_faces, clickable_faces, exits, bmodels) and numbers as values; other keys are free.

kind.description: room, corridor; void (no floor, such as a dome over a room); zone (an area inside another space that plays as its own); junction (a point: a road fork, a bridge head, a map-edge exit); outdoor: town, district, wild, water, road.

part_of.description: For a zone or void: the space it lies in or over.

mirror_of.description: Same shape as this space, mirrored; contents are its own.

mirror_axis.description: The line the shape is flipped across: ns (flips east and west) or ew (flips north and south).

area.description: Indoor floor area in million square units, when the size class is too coarse.

share.description: Outdoor: share of the map the zone covers (0 to 1).

extent.description: Rough size in map units, [width, depth].

shape.description: In words: octagon, L-shaped, winding slope, round basin.

where.description: Position in compass words or fractions of the map; never finer than the plan grid.

at.description: Where the space's bubble stands on the studio's plan, in map units (its middle): the Plan stage draws a space without a room there, as a dashed box of its `extent` (or its size class), with its links and goals; the Room tool drawn over it realises it. Not read by the build. Example: {id: space:crypt, kind: room, size: M, at: [3456, 320], extent: [768, 1024]}.

floor.description: Floor level against the plan's datum: a number, [low, high] for a sloping or uneven floor, or {level, range} when there is a typical level inside a range.

clear_height.description: Floor to ceiling: a number or [low, high].

top.description: For a void: its top above the floor of the space it lies over.

relief.description: How the floor behaves inside the space.

islands.description: Pillars or blocks big enough to walk round (loops the graph does not show).

kind.description: dais, alcove, colonnade, platform, wall_slot, balcony, pit, stair ...

safe.description: No fights here: always (true) or while a condition holds.

keep_clear.description: What the build must not put here.

backdrop.description: Seen but not walked: beyond the playable area.

theme.description: L2. A theme or kit from the shared library.

light.description: L2. unlit, dim, torchlit, bright; or lights per area.

fires.description: L1: lights that are part of the plan (camp fires, a beacon, braziers): a count.

density.description: Outdoor: how closely buildings or decorations stand.

coverage.description: Share of the zone under buildings (0 to 1).

building_gap.description: Typical gap between neighbouring buildings, map units.

buildings.description: Outdoor: buildings by type, tier and service. At L1 give services by count; ids and doors come with L2.

id.description: Names a building so states can lock or change it.

footprint_cells.description: Outdoor, L3: the ground the building covers in terrain cells, [front, depth]: front is the width of the side with the main door. Half cells allowed. A sketch.yml plot places it by its north-west corner and turns it by `facing`. For a `count` group whose members differ, a list of one [front, depth] per member in `index` order.

palette.description: L2. Decoration or prop families used here.

furniture.description: L2. What stands in the room, in words or kit names.

secret.description: The space is hidden until found.

motion.description: How a door or secret wall moves.

condition.description: The lock: what must hold to pass.

opened_by.description: What operates it when not a plain click: a lever, a pressure plate (id of a point of interest or set piece).

one_way.description: Passable only from `from` to `to` (a drop, or a shortcut that opens from one side).

opens_from.description: For a shortcut: the side it must first be opened from.

width.description: Map units, or `full` when a whole side is open.

crosses.description: Spaces it passes over or through without joining (a river under a bridge).

features.description: What stands along it: bridge, signposts, crates.

length_share.description: Roads: share of the map's road length.

to_any.description: A link that lands in one of several spaces.
